text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said it had decided to cut its main interest rate to 17.14 percent monthly from 18 percent, effective from Monday, in line with falling yield of short-term government securities.
-- The BNB said its foreign exchange reserves rose to $554.3 million at end-March from $445.5 million a month earlier. @
-- A 700 percent annual inflation in Bulgaria for this year assumed in the draft budget is not realistic as it could be reached by end-July, a National Statistics Institute expert said.

-- The private Bulgarian Investment bank (BIB) said it posted 1.74 billion levs net profit for last year under international accountancy standards. The bank's shareholders decided to admit a foreign investor as a new shareholder to contribute to a capital rise to 2.2 billion levs.
-- Foreign investment in Bulgaria amounted to $45.3 million in the first quarter, the country's Foreign Investment Agency said. Germany had the biggest share of investments with $9.8 million.
-- A Bulgarian delegation led by deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov is expected to take part in a joint meeting of G-24 and European Union countries on April 8-9 in Brussels.
A possible balance of payments support for Bulgaria is expected to be discussed at the meeting.
-- The Bulgarian customs officers said they had seized $500,000 worth of heroin hidden in a Turkish bus transiting from Turkey to Yugoslavia at the Bulgarian-Yugoslav border checkpoint of Kalotina.

-- The Bulgarian Telecommunication Company may receive a $40 million loan from the World Bank if projects for introduction of digital phone lines are implemented successfully, private Balkan news agency said.

-- Bulgaria's interim government authorised the Post and Telecommunication Committee to issue temporary six-month licences for radio- and TV broadcasts until a new Telecommunication Law is approved by the new parliament to assemble after April 19 election.

-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet decided to ban temporary imports of alchohol and tobacco in a bid to curb excise duty evasion as part of a funding accord with the International Monetary Fund. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
